experience.lesson: A prior cache attempt used 11 model turns, hit ambiguous/literal-edit rejections, and ran no tests before repeated-action stop. Use the supplied exact unique old/new recipe with the current source hash, make the bounded edit, then invoke the pinned verifier. Re-read only an anchor that actually changed.

A prior skill patch passed 10 old regression tests and was integrated, but independent source review found missing remaining-byte and marker-stability checks. Implement every explicit constraint; old verifier success alone does not prove the new requested behavior.

instruction: Fix merge() in merge_web_source.py. Archive sha(archive) then ZipFile(archive), and overlay sha(source) then shutil.copyfile(source,target), each reopen a pathname after checking its pin. A replaced pathname can substitute unverified bytes. For archives, open once, hash the opened seekable descriptor, rewind and pass that same descriptor to ZipFile; check descriptor stability around use. For each overlay, hash the exact bytes copied from one opened descriptor into a temporary file in the target directory, verify the expected hash and stable source before atomically replacing the target; clean up on failure. Preserve existing target permissions when replacing overlays; new targets retain normal creation permissions (0666 filtered by umask), without adding executable bits. Preserve sha(path), V4/V11 pins, existing archive/overlay path guards, valid union output and unchanged unrelated files. Change only this source and run the existing immutable verifier. This is source-level consistency, not original 0V14-14 or live WEB acceptance.
